target_customer: Consumers in Venezuela who order delivery and rides, plus small and medium merchants who sell through the app
problem: Venezuela lacked reliable delivery and ridesharing services and its dollarizing economy needed a local app that merchants and drivers could use.
business_model: delivery and ride commissions plus merchant services, ads and marketplace
product_category: super app for delivery, rides and commerce

founders.name: Vicente Zavarce
founders.background_notes: YC page: six years in growth marketing and user acquisition at Postmates and Getaround.

competitors.name: PedidosYa
competitors.what: Food delivery app that began in Venezuela in October 2020
competitors.funding_then: Part of Delivery Hero (not verified here)

technical_complexity.rationale: Delivery and rides apps are standard engineering but needed dark store logistics, local payments in dollars and bolivars and driver verification in a hard market.

defensibility.rationale: Local network of 100k plus drivers and 8,000 plus merchants per company claims, plus a first mover position in Venezuela; global players had weak presence there.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Sources conflict on whether Rappi and Uber operated in Venezuela in 2021; PedidosYa later said it would invest more there in 2022. Yummy kept expanding and bought Bolivia's Yaigo in October 2021.

market_need_then: Pandemic era demand for delivery and ridesharing and a dollarizing economy; Bloomberg Linea reported about 120,000 Caracas rides in one month in late 2021.

identity.logo: reported to have moved from green to the purple of hugo after a 2020 deal with hugo, per a Spanish language report; not confirmed by a second source
identity.visual_style: super app with several sub brands such as Yummy Rides and Wink
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly Spanish-first tone with the tagline Todo es Yummy.

branding.brand_signature: Tagline Todo es Yummy and one app with many sub brands
branding.community_and_virality: Large registered user base reported by the company (4M registered users); covered by TechCrunch, Forbes and Bloomberg Linea.

brand_strength.rationale: Familiar friendly name, well covered by press and a first mover in Venezuelan delivery, but the name is generic and was extended into non-food categories.

pivots.to: Super app adding rides, marketplace, travel and merchant tools
pivots.why: Company aims to be the super app of Venezuela, per its 2021 funding coverage.

outcome_analysis: Yummy became the main delivery and ridesharing app in Venezuela, raising a 4M seed in July 2021, an 18M Series A in October 2021 led by Anthos, and a 47M round in 2022. It claims 4M registered users, rides in 35 cities and multiple sub brands. It had planned expansion to Peru and Chile and bought Yaigo, but its current site lists Venezuela only, so the international expansion appears narrowed. No shutdown found.
notes: Series A of 18M USD is confirmed by TechCrunch, Bloomberg Linea, LAVCA and Contxto. Contxto says total capital was 22M USD after it; a later report says 69M USD total after the 47M round, whose exact date was not seen (2022). LatamList reported in October 2020 that hugo would acquire Yummy and said the deal would close in weeks; Appscrip also reported accepted terms. Closing was not confirmed and the company later raised independently, so no exit is recorded. One aggregator mentions an April 2025 acquisition offer, unverified. The YC page lists a 260 person team and headquarters in Los Angeles while most sources place operations in Caracas. The yummysuperapp.com page was truncated, so team and competitors there may be incomplete. Only one founder is listed by YC. Education not found. The seed investor list includes JAM Fund based on TechCrunch coverage of the Series A saying its founder invested in the seed.
